cat > /tmp/pr.md <<'EOF'
Closes #32.

## Summary

I checked every claim in the docs against the code (and its tests, where there are any), and then reorganized the docs. The README is now a landing page. The details live in focused pages under `docs/`. Each fact appears in one place, and other pages link to it.

| New page | Replaces |
|---|---|
| `docs/inputs.md` | README input table (the doc-sync tests now read it here) |
| `docs/workflows.md` | README examples: allowlists, bots, trigger phrase, comments only, output mode, `pr_number` |
| `docs/models.md` | README authentication, custom provider |
| `docs/extensions.md` | README pi extensions, pi-durable extensions, questions on GitHub |
| `docs/prompts.md` | README template section **and** `examples/prompt-templates.md` (now a one-line pointer) |
| `docs/threads.md` | README "Durable threads" and "Reading a thread" (these were duplicates) |
| `docs/security.md` | README security, token and git identity, question trust model |
| `docs/how-it-works.md` | README "How it works" and agent git hooks |

Each page puts its main point first (pyramid principle). The text uses short, active, imperative sentences (ASD-STE100 where it applies). CONTRIBUTING now has a short "Documentation style" section with these rules.

## Docs that were wrong (code unchanged)

- **The pit example made the run fail.** `github:cv/pit#v0.35.0   # pit's typescript tool` gives "is not an npm package spec or a path", because only lines that *start* with `#` are skipped. Comments now go on their own lines.
- **"Input is sanitized" claimed too much.** `sanitizeInput()` cleans only the trigger text, `/answer` replies, and question titles. The issue/PR title and body, the diff, and review comments reach the model unchanged.
- **`prompt_template`** replaces the *whole* first message, so the "commit and push your work" block is dropped. It applies only to the first message of a new thread. The docs now say this, list the missing `{{reviewComments}}` variable, and give the values for direct prompts.
- **`pr_number` on an existing thread** is sent as a follow-up, so the new diff is not included.
- **Custom `trigger_phrase`** also needs the `'@pi'` in the workflow's `if:` changed.
- **`prepare-commit-msg` hooks** (the agent's and this repo's) do nothing for `git commit -m`/`-F`, because git passes a commit source. I confirmed this in a scratch repo. Also, the agent's `commit-msg` hook rejects `feat!:`.
- **CONTRIBUTING:** CI runs `npm run check` (not just typecheck/lint/tests). Added the two dogfood workflows, which were missing. Tests use pi-ai's faux provider and real scratch git repos, not a "mocked pi SDK". Releases also move the `v2` tag.

## New test: `src/docs.test.ts`

- Every relative link and `#anchor` in every Markdown file resolves.
- `renderTemplate()` replaces every variable listed in `docs/prompts.md`.
- Every `extensions:` example in the docs parses. I checked that this fails on the old pit example.

`npm run check` passes: 315 tests (13 new), lint, knip, jscpd, and coverage.

## Open questions

1. Should the issue/PR **body and title** be sanitized as well? It is a one-line change in `run-context.ts`. I only documented the current behavior.
2. Should `extensions` accept **trailing `# comments`**? Stripping `\s+#.*$` would be safe, because specs never contain whitespace.
3. Moving the input table out of the README means the Marketplace page no longer shows the inputs. It is linked from the docs table. If you want it back in the README, I can move it back and point the tests at it again.
EOF
gh pr create --base main --head docs/32-documentation-cleanup --title "docs: reorganize and verify the documentation" --body-file /tmp/pr.md 2>&1 | tail -2
